description:
We are a real-life, science-loving family (a mother, a father, and a son) participating together in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are passionate about STEAM, space exploration, and using NASA's open data to solve real-world challenges. From creative design and storytelling to software development, we combine our different skills right from our own home

As a family unit, we bring a solid foundation in Graphic/UI Design, Project Management, Software Development, and Science Communication.
summary:
Our team developed an interactive, bilingual (English/Arabic) web application titled 'AstroHeritage: The Museum of Forgotten Space Artifacts'. We addressed the challenge by shifting the narrative around NASA’s discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars from 'space debris' to valuable 'space heritage'. The platform features an immersive 3D virtual environment with an orbital particle network and an artifact map, bringing the history of off-world artifacts to life using NASA NSSDC archive imagery and data.

To deeply engage diverse audiences, we integrated age-tiered Space Archaeology Labs tailored for different age groups (Little Explorers, Junior Astronauts, and Heritage Protectors). These labs offer interactive, hands-on STEAM activities designed to teach sustainability and preserve humanity's legacy in space.

This project is important because it bridges the gap between traditional archaeology and space science. It educates the next generation about sustainable space exploration and inspires the public to appreciate and protect our historical legacy across the solar system.
details:
"AstroHeritage: The Museum of Forgotten Space Artifacts" is a fully interactive, bilingual (English/Arabic) web platform designed to preserve and educate about off-world artifacts. The project functions as a unified learning environment divided into two main modules:

  1. Space Museum (Gallery & Map): Users navigate an interactive artifact map featuring distinct Moon and Mars galleries. Each artifact (e.g., Apollo 11 Descent Stage, Perseverance Parachute) opens in an immersive 3D-styled display case ("Artifact Registry") with an Environmental HUD showing surface temperature, hazards, and a Structural Integrity Meter.
    • Little Explorers (5-8 yrs): Rover assembly puzzles and space coloring activities.
    • Junior Astronauts (9-13 yrs): Martian dust-sweeping simulations and historical timeline reconstruction.
    • Heritage Leaders (14-18 yrs): Advanced modules like "Space Hieroglyphics" (binary code decoding), power management simulators (balancing heat, comms, and sensors), radar coordinate scanning, and heritage classification law debates.

Benefits & Intended Impact The primary benefit is transforming the concept of "space debris" into "space heritage" through gamified, cross-generational learning. By grouping activities by age and cognitive level, the platform benefits diverse audiences—from young children discovering space to teens engaging in complex physics and ethical debates. The intended impact is to foster a sense of global responsibility for off-world preservation, ensuring future generations value the historical significance of our early steps into the cosmos.

Tools, Coding Languages, and Software Used

  • Core Architecture: Developed as a unified web application using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (Vanilla JS).
  • Styling & UI: Tailwind CSS for responsive layouts, combined with custom CSS glassmorphism, animations (pulse, spin, holographic scans), and orbital particle networks rendered via HTML5 Canvas.
  • Interactive Elements: JavaScript for state management, interactive modal logic, and dynamic DOM manipulation (e.g., the interactive dust sweeper, binary decoder, and power sliders).
  • Data Visualization: Chart.js integrated for "Lifespan Analysis" (Expected vs. Actual lifespan of artifacts).
  • Assets & Fonts: Google Fonts (Cairo for Arabic, Inter/Orbitron for English/Tech aesthetics), Phosphor Icons, and FontAwesome. NASA NSSDC imagery was utilized for artifact visualization.

Creativity & Team Considerations The creativity of AstroHeritage lies in its dual-identity: it is both a historical archive and a futuristic simulator. We designed the UI to mimic a "Space Archaeologist Dashboard," complete with glowing neon accents, holographic loading screens, and scanning radars, which deeply immerses the user in the role.

Our team, "Family Space," prioritized accessibility and inclusivity. We engineered a seamless bilingual toggle (English/Arabic) with full Right-to-Left (RTL) support to serve the MENA region. Furthermore, the single-page application (SPA) architecture with iframe-based module isolation ensures the platform is lightweight, fast, and easily scalable for future NASA hackathons or educational deployments.
